thread.title: Walt Disney Streaming Services Investments Lose Big Money |

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: Walt Disney Streaming Services Investments Lose Big Money |

organizations.name: walt disney streaming services investments lose big money | walt disney

text:
Walt Disney ( DIS ) revealed in a regulatory filing Friday that it lost more than $1 billion on video streaming investments in the last fiscal year. But on Monday, Disney's Black Panther and the Netflix ( NFLX ) movie Roma earned Oscar nominations for best picture, showcasing the disruptive potential of Netflix and Disney streaming services.
Disney's filing showed a $580 million loss on equity investments in the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, driven by higher losses from its Hulu investment. It also lost $469 million on direct-to-consumer services, led by the BAMtech streaming technology underpinning ESPN+.
ESPN+ added 568,000 new subscribers on Friday-Saturday alone, Disney's sports network said Tuesday, as customers watched the premiere of UFC Fight Night on the streaming service.
Disney streaming investments are only going to increase in 2019.
 Disney CEO Bob Iger plans to show off the Disney+ streaming service in April as he fends off main rivals Netflix and Amazon ( AMZN ), as well as new competition.
The Disney streaming service will include original movies and TV shows from various Disney brands including Marvel, the studio behind Black Panther.
Disney's Black Panther Gets Oscar Big Picture Nomination Meanwhile, Disney's Black Panther, a mega box-office hit, became the first superhero movie to land a best picture Oscar nomination Monday. Rival Netflix scored its first best picture nomination with Roma. The nominations mark a milestone moment for video streaming companies, which are reshaping old ways of doing business in Hollywood.
Disney Stock Technical Analysis Disney stock fell 0.4% to 110.64 on the stock market today . Shares have hit resistance at their 50-day line after rebounding with the stock market since late December.
Netflix stock fell 4.11% after sinking 4% Friday following weak Netflix earnings guidance. Amazon gave up 3.8%.
Disney Streaming Service Confronts Old, New Rivals The mixed Disney news comes just weeks after Sinclair Broadcast Group ( SBGI ) and Comcast ( CMCSA )-owned NBC Universal launched or announced free, ad-supported streaming services.
But Walmart ( WMT ) reportedly ditched plans for a new service to focus on its Vudu streaming platform.
Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Disney-controlled Hulu, which dominate movie and TV show streaming, face off a growing number of competitors.
Companies from Apple ( AAPL ) and AT&T ( T ) to Costco ( COST ) are preparing or mulling entries in subscription video services.
